Anything from Community season four. Yes, even the puppet episode. Yes, even the freaky friday episode. Yes, even the one with Brie Larson. Yes, even whichever episode of season four you thought was the good one. Even that one.

On it's own, Community season 4 isn't terrible television. If it had been a different show, I might have watched it every now and then. It would be an amusing sitcom with some good actors. It would be a show that tried a little too hard to be weird, but it was still pretty decent. I wouldn't record this show or anything, but on the other hand I wouldn't turn it off if it happened to be on.

The problem was that it was Community. One of those great bits of television that remind you that the medium can make something that has meaning...which is what art should be. Dan Harmon cracked the code when it came to sitcom writing. His idea of the "story circle" where the half hour could be broken down along the Joseph Campbell monomyth structure, led to a show where the episodes had actual meaning. There was also an emotional component to the show that made it one of the top five sitcoms ever written. If it had come out in the age of network television, people would talk about Community in the same breath as Cheers, Seinfeld, or Newhart. Instead it was in an age of declining viewerships.

I think the biggest impact will be, like Arrested Development, on future writers entering television. It'll be a show where you want to breakdown the plot and understand how it was constructed.
